senses.gloss: To recognize the difference between two similar things.
examples: It takes practice to *discern* real leather from a good imitation.
The judges *discerned* a clear difference between the two performances.
Readers have trouble *discerning* fact from opinion online.

senses.gloss: To dismiss someone from a job or from military service.
examples: He was *discharged* from the Army after four years.
A company may *discharge* an employee for theft.
Having been dishonorably *discharged*, he had trouble finding work.

senses.gloss: To send out liquid, gas, or waste.
examples: The plant *discharges* wastewater into the river.
The factory *discharged* chemicals for years before anyone noticed.
Pipes along the roof were *discharging* steam into the cold air.

senses.gloss: To fire a gun.
examples: It is illegal to *discharge* a firearm inside city limits.
The officer *discharged* his weapon twice.
The rifle went off, *discharging* a round into the ceiling.

senses.gloss: To train someone, or yourself, to follow rules and control behavior.
examples: Good parents *discipline* their children with clear, steady rules.
She *disciplined* herself to write for an hour every morning.
He has never been good at *disciplining* his spending.

senses.gloss: To treat something as unimportant or unlikely to be true.
senses.ru: сбрасывать со счетов, не принимать в расчёт
examples: Don't *discount* the possibility that she was right all along.
Investigators *discounted* the witness's story after checking the timeline.
You shouldn't be *discounting* his experience just because he is young.

senses.gloss: To see or make a fine difference between things that are nearly alike.
examples: A trained ear can *discriminate* between the two notes.
The children *discriminated* the shapes by color alone.
The filter is good at *discriminating* spam from real mail.

senses.gloss: To hide a feeling, fact, or quality so that others do not notice it.
examples: He could not *disguise* his disappointment.
She *disguised* her accent for the interview.
All that sauce is just *disguising* the taste of old fish.

senses.gloss: To officially remove someone from a job.
examples: The school *dismissed* two teachers after the investigation.
An employer cannot *dismiss* you for taking sick leave.
He is suing the company for *dismissing* him without warning.

senses.gloss: To tell a group of people that they may leave.
examples: The teacher *dismisses* the class at three o'clock.
The principal *dismissed* the students early because of the storm.
We were *dismissed* as soon as the drill ended.

senses.gloss: To show a feeling, quality, or skill through the way you behave.
examples: He rarely *displays* any emotion at work.
The crew *displayed* remarkable calm during the emergency.
She has been *displaying* real leadership since the merger.

senses.gloss: To officially end a company, a partnership, or a legal arrangement.
examples: The two founders decided to *dissolve* their partnership.
The judge *dissolved* the order a week later.
After *dissolving* the company, they sold off the equipment.

senses.gloss: To suddenly start crying or laughing and be unable to stop.
examples: She *dissolved* into tears when she heard the news.
The whole room *dissolves* into laughter whenever he tells that story.
He was *dissolving* into giggles in the middle of the ceremony.

senses.gloss: To manage to see or hear something that is hard to make out.
examples: In the fog we could barely *distinguish* the shoreline.
She *distinguished* three figures moving along the ridge.
Even with binoculars he had trouble *distinguishing* the bird against the rocks.

senses.gloss: To do something so well that people notice and admire you.
examples: Cadets who *distinguish* themselves are offered command posts.
She *distinguished* herself as a trial lawyer before turning forty.
He has *distinguished* himself in three different fields.

senses.gloss: To spread something evenly over an area or a surface.
examples: *Distribute* the weight evenly across both axles.
The paint was not *distributed* evenly, so the wall looks streaky.
One vent *distributes* warm air to the whole upstairs.

senses.gloss: To move or touch something so that it is no longer as it was.
examples: Nothing in the room had been *disturbed*.
Please do not *disturb* the nests along the trail.
The dog kept *disturbing* the neatly raked gravel.

senses.gloss: To skip a class or an obligation you are supposed to attend (informal).
examples: They *ditched* class and drove out to the lake.
Don't *ditch* practice again.
He got caught *ditching* school twice in April.

senses.gloss: To drop steeply and fast.
examples: Stock prices *dive* every time the rumor resurfaces.
The plane *dived* toward the runway and pulled up at the last second.
Temperatures have been *diving* since the front moved through.

senses.gloss: To swim underwater using breathing equipment.
examples: They *dive* off the Keys every summer.
We *dived* to forty feet to see the wreck.
He spent the week *diving* with a local guide.

senses.gloss: For a business to start selling new kinds of products or move into new activities.
examples: Small stores have to *diversify* to survive.
The farm *diversified* into cheese and weekend tourism.
The company has been *diversifying* away from print for a decade.

senses.gloss: To find how many times one number goes into another.
examples: *Divide* twelve by four and you get three.
She *divided* the bill by the number of guests.
*Dividing* by zero is not allowed.

senses.gloss: To make people disagree strongly with one another.
examples: The issue *divides* the whole country.
The proposal *divided* the board for months.
It is a question that has *divided* families.

senses.gloss: To take money out of someone's pay as a penalty.
examples: They *docked* his pay for coming in late.
The company will *dock* you an hour if you miss the meeting.
She complained about being *docked* for a sick day.

senses.gloss: To avoid a question, a duty, or a payment by being clever about it.
examples: The senator *dodged* the question twice.
Some firms *dodge* taxes through offshore accounts.
He spent the whole year *dodging* his responsibilities.

senses.gloss: To lower the official rank, rating, or classification of something.
examples: Forecasters *downgraded* the hurricane to a tropical storm.
Analysts may *downgrade* the stock after the earnings call.
The agency has *downgraded* the country's credit rating twice.

senses.gloss: To order someone by law to serve in the armed forces.
examples: His father was *drafted* in 1968.
The government could *draft* men under the age of thirty.
Thousands of young men were being *drafted* every month.

senses.gloss: To pick a player for a professional sports team.
examples: Teams *draft* college players every June.
The Knicks *drafted* him in the second round.
She was *drafted* straight out of her junior year.

senses.gloss: To move something on a screen by holding it down with the mouse or a finger.
examples: *Drag* the file into the folder.
She *dragged* the photo onto the desktop.
You can reorder the list by *dragging* the rows.

senses.gloss: For time or an event to pass slowly and tediously.
examples: The meeting *dragged* until almost seven.
Rehearsals *drag* when nobody is prepared.
With the storm outside, the whole afternoon was *dragging*.

senses.gloss: To clean a wound and cover it with a bandage.
examples: A nurse *dressed* the cut and sent him home.
*Dress* the wound twice a day.
The burn is still being *dressed* every morning.

senses.gloss: To put oil, vinegar, or sauce on a salad.
examples: *Dress* the salad right before serving.
She *dressed* the greens with lemon and olive oil.
I like *dressing* the salad at the table so it doesn't wilt.

senses.gloss: For a liquid to fall or run in a thin, uneven stream.
examples: Water *dribbled* down the wall all night.
Juice *dribbles* out of the carton if you tip it.
He wiped the paint that was *dribbling* off the brush.

senses.gloss: To move through life or from place to place with no plan or purpose.
senses.ru: плыть по течению, слоняться без цели
examples: He *drifted* from job to job for years.
Some students just *drift* through their first year of college.
She spent her twenties *drifting* around Europe.

senses.gloss: To teach something by making people repeat it many times.
examples: The teacher *drills* the class on irregular verbs.
Sergeants *drilled* the recruits for six weeks.
We have been *drilling* the same play all week.

senses.gloss: For light rain to fall in very fine drops.
examples: It *drizzled* off and on all morning.
If it *drizzles*, the game goes on anyway.
It was *drizzling* when we left the stadium.

senses.gloss: To stop doing or discussing something, or to cancel it.
examples: The prosecutor *dropped* the charges.
Can we *drop* the subject?
She is thinking about *dropping* her chemistry class.

senses.gloss: To give someone or something a nickname or label.
examples: The press *dubbed* him the Comeback Kid.
Reporters *dub* every new scandal something-gate.
The storm, *dubbed* Snowmageddon, shut the city down for a week.

senses.gloss: To avoid a question or a responsibility.
examples: The mayor *ducked* the question about taxes.
You can't *duck* this decision forever.
He has been *ducking* reporters all week.

senses.gloss: To suddenly end a romantic relationship with someone (informal).
examples: She *dumped* him over the phone.
If he keeps lying, she will *dump* him.
He was *dumped* two weeks before the wedding.

senses.gloss: To jump up and push the ball down through the basket.
examples: He *dunked* over two defenders.
She can *dunk* with either hand.
He has *dunked* twice already this quarter.

senses.gloss: To sprinkle a fine powder lightly over something.
examples: *Dust* the cake with powdered sugar before serving.
She *dusted* the pan with flour.
Snow had *dusted* the fields overnight.

senses.gloss: To move something, or yourself, slowly and carefully into place.
examples: He *eased* the car into the garage.
*Ease* the board into the slot; don't force it.
She was *easing* herself out of the chair when the phone rang.

senses.gloss: To repeat or agree with what someone else has said.
examples: Her report *echoes* what the engineers said last year.
Several senators *echoed* the same complaint.
The article is *echoing* arguments made a decade ago.

senses.gloss: To become so much better or more important that someone else seems small by comparison.
examples: A younger rival can *eclipse* you in a single season.
Her second novel *eclipsed* the first.
Streaming has *eclipsed* cable in almost every market.

senses.gloss: To cut and arrange film, video, or recorded sound into a finished piece.
examples: She *edits* documentaries for a living.
The trailer was *edited* in two days.
He is *editing* the wedding video this weekend.

senses.gloss: To be in charge of a newspaper, magazine, or book and decide what goes in it.
examples: She *edits* the city's oldest weekly.
He *edited* the paper for eleven years.
The volume was *edited* by two historians.

senses.gloss: To force someone to leave a place.
senses.ru: выдворять, выгонять; удалять (с поля, из зала)
examples: Security *ejected* two fans in the third inning.
An umpire can *eject* a player for arguing.
He was *ejected* from the building by two guards.
